newsitem.title: USA: Wash. state Senate GOP unveils $19 bln budget plan.
newsitem.headline: Wash. state Senate GOP unveils $19 bln budget plan.

text.p: Washington state Senate Republicans on Monday rolled out a $19.1 billion budget plan for the 1997-1999 biennium that calls for a reserve of $370 million and $500 million in tax relief.

"We avoided using temporary savings to fund ongoing programs," state Senate Ways and Means Committee Chairman James West said in a statement. "We've used sound budget principles to build a framework for the future."
Washington Gov. Gary Locke, a Democrat, said the Senate proposal was a "good starting point" for budget negotiations.

The Senate GOP budget boosts education funding, and includes nearly $500 million in tax relief for property owners and employers, a 3.0 percent cost-of-living increase for teachers, faculty and state employees, and $20 million in additional funding for juvenile justice system reforms.

Earlier this month, Locke proposed a $19.2 billion operating budget for the 1997-1999 biennium. Locke's budget called for a reserve of $304 million and would provide $311 million in tax reductions for homeowners and businesses during the next two years.

"I commend Senator West for his efforts to make education his top priority, as I did in the budget I released three weeks ago. We also agree on the importance of sustainable budgets," Locke said in a statement. "This creates a good starting point for working out our differences."
Locke urged senators to provide more assistance to rural schools and to address the state's water crisis.
The Senate GOP spending plan is expected to be considering by the Senate Ways and Means Committee on Tuesday and by the full Senate on Wednesday.
